readme:
# JobScout24.ch Scraper - Swiss Job Board Data Extraction

## What you get

Job postings from JobScout24.ch, one row per job, as JSON, CSV, Excel or through the API. This actor collects jobs in Switzerland from one of the larger Swiss general job boards:

- Job title, company, city, canton, employment type and workload percentage
- Posting date, salary text when the ad shows one, and a remote or hybrid flag
- Full description as plain text and Markdown, plus the requirements list
- Apply link, apply email and contact person details when the ad publishes them
- Company profile data: description, rating, social links and benefits

## Input example

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["Developer"],
  "region": "basel",
  "category": "it",
  "includeJobDetails": true,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 20
}
```

## Output example

One row from a search with `includeJobDetails` off (fields the listing does not show stay `null`):

```json

  "id": "10453788",
  "title": "SAP Entwickler*in",
```

---

JobScout24.ch carries listings in German, French, and Italian across every sector - IT, engineering, finance, healthcare, hospitality, logistics, and more - making it a strong complement to the JobCloud family (jobs.ch, jobup.ch) for comprehensive Swiss market coverage.

---

## Features

- Three input modes: **searchQueries** (keywords) · **directUrls** (single-job re-scrape / still-alive checks) · **searchQuery** (legacy single keyword, backward compatible)
- Regional targeting: 11 Swiss regions including Zurich, Bern, Basel, Romandie, Tessin, Graubunden, Wallis, and Remote
- Category filtering: 15 career categories from IT and Engineering to Healthcare, Legal, and Hospitality
- Employment type filter: Full-time, Part-time, Temporary, Apprenticeship, Internship
- Sort order control: `newest` (Currentness), `relevance`, `title`, `company`, `location` via server-side `sortby` URL parameter
- Job status detection on direct-URL mode: `online`, `expired`, `unknown`. Job pages that are gone or offline (404, 410, "job not found" or expired pages) produce no row and are not charged; the run still succeeds and the final status message tells you how many URLs were skipped
- Top listing flag: identifies promoted placements in SERP results
- Workload range extraction: `workload_min` and `workload_max` percentages (Swiss standard)
- Full description in plain text and snippet formats; structured requirements array
- Company enrichment: description, rating, review count, social media URLs, benefits list
- Contact extraction: salutation, first name, last name, email, phone, position from detail pages
- Apply URL and apply email extracted from detail pages
- Fast SERP-only mode: `includeJobDetails: false` skips detail pages for bulk collection
- Multi-query deduplication across all keyword runs in a single actor invocation
- Concurrent detail fetching (5 workers, batches of 50) for efficient throughput
- Automatic stronger connections when the website blocks a request, so runs finish instead of stopping
- 128 MB memory footprint; written in Go for low compute-unit cost

---

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client - Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/jobscout24-ch-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `jobscout24-ch-scraper` to scrape up to 50 IT jobs in the Zurich region from JobScout24.ch. Return results as a table with title, company, location, and apply URL."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) will receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

---

## Sample input

**Keyword search (standard mode):**

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["Softwareentwickler", "Projektleiter"],
  "region": "zurich",
  "category": "it",
  "sortBy": "newest",
  "includeJobDetails": true,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 50,
  "maxResults": 100
}
```

**Direct URL mode (re-scrape / still-alive checks):**

```json
{
  "directUrls": [
    "https://www.jobscout24.ch/de/job/10226990",
    "https://www.jobscout24.ch/en/job/10189234"
  ]
}
```

**SERP-only mode (bulk collection, no detail pages):**

```json
{
  "searchQueries": ["Verkäufer", "Logistiker"],
  "includeJobDetails": false,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 200
}
```

## Input fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | string[] | - | One or more keywords. Each runs as a separate search; results are deduplicated. |
| `searchQuery` | string | - | Single keyword (legacy, backward compatible). Use `searchQueries` for new integrations. |
| `directUrls` | string[] | - | Job detail page URLs to scrape directly, skipping search. Use for still-alive checks or targeted re-scrapes. |
| `location` | string | City or place, for example `Bern`. Enforced on every job (the site search does not narrow by place on its own). Jobs whose place cannot be determined are kept unless the job page shows another place or canton. | empty |
| `radius` | integer | Kilometres around `location` (empty or 0 = the default of 25 km; the place itself and its districts such as `Bern 14` are always kept). Distances use built-in coordinates of about 60 Swiss towns; for other places the canton decides. | 25 |
| `region` | enum | All regions | Swiss region filter: `zurich`, `bern`, `basel`, `aargau`, `ostschweiz`, `zentralschweiz`, `romandie`, `tessin`, `graubunden`, `wallis`, `remote` |
| `category` | enum | All categories | Career category filter: `it`, `engineering`, `finance`, `sales`, `marketing`, `hr`, `healthcare`, `education`, `hospitality`, `construction`, `logistics`, `administration`, `management`, `legal`, `customer-service` |
| `employmentType` | enum | All types | Employment type filter: `full-time`, `part-time`, `temporary`, `apprenticeship`, `internship` |
| `sortBy` | enum | `newest` | Sort order: `newest` (most recently posted first), `relevance` (JobScout24 default ranking), `title` (job title A-Z), `company` (company name A-Z), `location` (place of work A-Z). |
| `postedWithinDays` | int | `0` (off) | Only jobs posted within the last N days. Day granularity (the site shows ages like `New`, `1 d`), boundary inclusive: `1` keeps today and yesterday. Applied server-side and before detail fetch and billing. Jobs without a date are kept. |
| `maxAgeHours` | int | `0` (off) | Co-canonical with `postedWithinDays`; if both are set the stricter wins. With job details on, the exact posting time is checked before billing; in SERP-only mode it is evaluated per calendar day (Europe/Zurich) because the site has no hour-level ages. |
| `titleFilter` | string | empty (off) | Comma-separated terms, case-insensitive substring OR-match on the job title (e.g. `Laborant, Chemiker, QC`). Applied before the detail fetch and billing. |
| `includeJobDetails` | bool | `true` | Visit each job's detail page for full description, contact info, apply URL, and company data. Set `false` for fast SERP-only collection. |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | int | `100` | Per-keyword result cap. Set to `0` for unlimited per query. |
| `maxResults` | int | `0` | Global cap across all queries. Set to `0` for unlimited. |

---

## Output fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | JobScout24 job ID |
| `title` | string | Job title |
| `company` | string or null | Hiring company name |
| `location` | string | City or area |
| `country` | string | Always `CH` |
| `canton` | string or null | Swiss canton code (e.g. `ZH`, `BE`, `GE`) |
| `job_status` | string or null | `online` / `expired` / `unknown`. Populated in direct-URL mode. Offline or gone job pages are skipped (no row, no charge). |
| `top_listing` | bool or null | `true` for promoted placements |
| `employment_type` | string or null | `full-time`, `part-time`, `temporary`, etc. |
| `workload_min` | number or null | Minimum workload percentage |
| `workload_max` | number or null | Maximum workload percentage |
| `remote_option` | string or null | Remote work availability: `remote` (fully remote), `hybrid` (home office or mobile working mentioned in the ad), or null when the ad says nothing |
| `salary_text` | string or null | Salary as displayed (e.g. `CHF 90'000 - 110'000`) |
| `description_snippet` | string or null | First 500 characters of the description |
| `description_full` | string or null | Complete job description text |
| `description_md` | string or null | Job description converted to Markdown |
| `requirements` | string[] | Bullet points under the ad's profile / requirements headings (e.g. "Dein Profil", "Das bringst du mit") |
| `posted_at` | string or null | Posting date. `YYYY-MM-DD` (Swiss day) when the site only gives a day ("heute", "gestern", "vor 3 Tagen"), full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when it gives a time |
| `expires_at` | string or null | ISO 8601 expiry date |
| `source_url` | string | Direct URL to the job listing |
| `source_platform` | string | Always `jobscout24.ch` |
| `contact_salutation` | string or null | Contact person salutation (Herr, Frau) when the ad names it |
| `contact_firstname` | string or null | Contact person first name |
| `contact_lastname` | string or null | Contact person last name |
| `contact_email` | string or null | Contact person email address |
| `contact_phone` | string or null | Contact person phone number |
| `contact_position` | string or null | Contact person job title |
| `contact_raw` | string or null | Raw contact text from the end of the ad (the contact person block, "Fragen?", "Ansprechperson", "Kontakt") |
| `apply_url` | string or null | Direct application URL |
| `apply_email` | string or null | Application email address |
| `company_url` | string or null | Company profile URL on JobScout24 |
| `company_description` | string or null | Company description text |
| `company_rating` | number or null | Company rating score |
| `company_review_count` | number or null | Number of company reviews |
| `company_social_urls` | object or null | Social media URLs keyed by platform (e.g. `linkedin`) |
| `company_benefits` | string[] or null | Company-offered benefits list |
| `search_query` | string or null | The keyword that returned this listing |
| `scraped_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp of when the item was scraped |

Contact fields are read from the contact block at the end of the ad text, so they are filled only when the ad names a contact person, phone or email. You are responsible for using the data lawfully, including the GDPR/DSGVO, national data-protection laws and unfair-competition rules (e.g. UWG) for marketing and outreach.

## Pricing (Pay-per-event)

Until November 18, 2026 each job costs $0.003.

From November 18, 2026:

| Event | Price | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `apify-actor-start` | $0.001 | Every run, once |
| `job-serp-result` | $0.003 | A job taken from the search results (details off, or the job page could not be read) |
| `job-detail-result` | $0.0045 | A job with full details read from its job page (the default) |

Job pages that are gone or offline produce no row and cost nothing. If you set a maximum cost per run, the run stops saving jobs once that limit is reached and ends as succeeded.

---|---|---|
| `apify-actor-start` | One-time run start fee (a tiny amount) | Every run, once |
| `apify-default-dataset-item` | One price per result | Once for every job saved to the dataset |

Every saved job costs the same per-result price, whether or not the full job page was read. Job pages that are gone or offline produce no row and cost nothing. If you set a maximum cost per run, the run stops saving jobs once that limit is reached and ends as succeeded.

---

## FAQ

### What happens if the website blocks the run?

The actor switches to stronger connections on its own. If the website still refuses every connection, the run ends cleanly with a plain status message and no jobs are charged for pages it could not read.

## Changelog

- 3.5.2: proxy ladder (datacenter, residential, unblocker) with bounded timeouts; exits cleanly without charge when the site blocks every tier.
- 3.5.2: the proxy is now chosen automatically; a proxyConfiguration value sent through the API is ignored.
- 3.5.3: connection layer updated (exact traffic accounting for compressed pages, full datacenter, residential and unblocker fallback chain); added a Job Listings table view in the Output tab.
- 3.5.4: connections now start on the datacenter level, then residential (Switzerland), then unblocker (no direct connection first); new `location` and `radius` inputs, and `region` is now checked on every job, so a Bern search no longer returns jobs from all over Switzerland; `posted_at` from search-only rows (relative dates like "heute", "gestern", "vor 3 Tagen") is a plain date (YYYY-MM-DD, Swiss day); with job details on, the job page gives an exact time, so `posted_at` stays a full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
- 3.5.5: changelog wording for `posted_at` corrected (no code change).
- 3.5.6: fixed a search with a `location` (for example "Bern") and no `radius` that returned no jobs at all. Without a radius the actor now uses 25 km around the place, so nearby towns such as Köniz or Ostermundigen are kept. Place names like "Region Bern", "Bümpliz (Bern)", "CH-3000 Bern" or "Homeoffice / Bern" are now recognised, and a place the actor does not know is never a reason to drop a job. If the place filter removes every job, the run status now says how many jobs were found and that none were inside the radius.
- 3.5.7: the place filter now knows about 10,000 Swiss towns and villages, so jobs in far-away places (for example Sursee or Rolle when you search Bern with 25 km) are no longer delivered or charged. The actor now keeps reading result pages until it has your requested number of jobs inside the area, instead of stopping early with only a few. When jobs were skipped because they are outside the radius, the run status says how many, for example "3 jobs delivered; 65 outside 25 km of Bern skipped."
- 3.5.8: places written like "Bönigen b. Interlaken", "Bönigen bei Interlaken" or "Bönigen (Interlaken)" are now judged by their own place first, so they are no longer kept as if they were in the bigger town next to them. When some jobs are dropped after their detail page was read (wrong place or too old), the actor now reads more result pages to replace them, so you get your requested number of jobs whenever enough matching jobs exist. Vague places such as "Deutschschweiz" or "Romandie" are still kept, never charged beyond your maximum.

If this actor works well for you, a rating on Apify helps other users find it.
